### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via HookSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 300f740f1b79b016d7446bb8e88554ff380dbde1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `542622693d6cf27c015674c33770aaad12b88fa8` — the merge of head `0faa19a120690de516114c22ea9a9f2a12f41af8` into base `300f740f1b79b016d7446bb8e88554ff380dbde1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 542622693d6cf27c015674c33770aaad12b88fa8 && git checkout 542622693d6cf27c015674c33770aaad12b88fa8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 300f740f1b79b016d7446bb8e88554ff380dbde1 0faa19a120690de516114c22ea9a9f2a12f41af8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 300f740f1b79b016d7446bb8e88554ff380dbde1 && git merge --no-ff 0faa19a120690de516114c22ea9a9f2a12f41af8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 300f740f1b79b016d7446bb8e88554ff380dbde1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 300f740f1b79b016d7446bb8e88554ff380dbde1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0faa19a120690de516114c22ea9a9f2a12f41af8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md + packages/lint/src/validate-null-guards.ts (ledger flow row point 3, `truthGuards`, `provenNonNullKeys`, `findUnguardedNullableOperands`), packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts (`checkNullGuards` ≈L2486, the flow null-guard block ≈L2921-L2977, the trigger-gate call ≈L3106, the `decision` call ≈L3211, the edge call ≈L3341, the hook `condition` loop ≈L4006-L4050), packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts (`resolveFlowTriggerKind`), packages/lint/scripts/check-doc-formula-expressions.mjs (`judge`, the `hook-record-condition` entry of `SPEC_EXAMPLE_SLOTS`), skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md (≈L99-L125 and the flow-conditions note ≈L399-L407), skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md (frontmatter pointer to objectstack-formula), skills/objectstack-automation/evals/ (all three files), scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs (the row for the approvals reference), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.erasedArmMark-9830.test.tsx (hand-copied describe text). Cited code read on `origin/main` `300f740f`. The merge base is `f8c3ecc4`, and none of the cited files moved between the two. The PR is `247bd53c1` plus a merge of main (`0faa19a12`). The rest of the diff, .changeset/31206-approval-and-hook-amount-null-guards.md and the regenerated content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx, is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #31206 (body, triage 2026-11-07T17:55Z, claim 2026-11-08T00:53Z), the PR body, its file list (4 files, +20 / -4), the net diff against the merge base, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs, read 2026-11-08T02:04Z: 42 runs. 14 success, 7 skipped, 21 in progress, none failed.
- Green: `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Documentation Links`.
- Still running: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, the two scoped lint jobs, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, all eight `Test Core` shards, and `Live E2E UI`.
- The gates that judge this diff most directly (`check:docs`, `check:generated`, `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:skill-examples` and the token ratchet) sit in jobs that are still running. This record does not stand in for them.

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

- **No accept set moves.** RIGHT. hook.zod.ts changes the `@example` tag and the `.describe()` string of `condition`. The schema stays `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema.optional()`. No parse, refine or default changes.
- **Published description text changes.** RIGHT, and as a patch. The new string goes into the JSON-schema projection the metadata admin serves and into hook.mdx L39. No other committed artifact carries the string. A repo grep for "hook runs only when TRUE" finds only hook.zod.ts, hook.mdx, the lint registry's `why` text (a prefix, still true) and one UI test fixture (see ③).
- **The skill's approval example now passes the publish-time null-guard rule on both doors.** RIGHT. Traced:
  - `resolveFlowTriggerKind`: `triggerType: 'record-after-update'` starts with `record-`, so the kind is `record_change`. `nullGuardObject` is therefore `'opportunity'`, and the gate runs whenever the app declares `opportunity.amount` nullable.
  - The start condition is the trigger gate (`type === 'start'`, top-level graph), judged with no presumption. `record.amount != null && record.amount > 100000`: the `&&` visit hands the right conjunct `truthGuards(left)`, and `!=` against the null literal yields the key `record.amount`. The `>` operand is guarded. No finding.
  - `provenNonNullKeys(startConditionSource, …)` runs the same `truthGuards` and returns `{record.amount}`. That set is passed as `presumed` to every edge (`afterStart: true`, every graph) and every `decision` slot.
  - Edges `e1` (`> 100000`), `e4` (`> 500000`) and `e5` (`<= 500000`) all resolve, through `fieldOf`, to the key `record.amount`. That key is in the starting guard set of `visit`, so `report` returns early for each one. No finding.
  - The runtime publish gate (`perWriteSnapshotEntrance`) leaves `rootScope.provable` false, so `nullGuardBare` is empty. The guard is spelled `record.amount`, not bare, so the proof does not need a bare name and still yields `{record.amount}`. Both `os validate` and the publish gate accept the flow. This is exactly the "spell that guard `record.x != null`" instruction in ledger point 3 and formula SKILL.md L404-L406.
  - The `decision` node `needs_director` carries no config, so no `decision` slot is judged. Its routing is on `e4` / `e5`, which are edges.
- **The hook example now passes the hook-condition gate.** RIGHT. `record.status == 'closed' && record.amount != null && record.amount > 1000` parses left-associative, so the last conjunct's guard set is `truthGuards(record.status == 'closed' && record.amount != null)`, which is `{} ∪ {record.amount}`. Equality is never flagged. The hook loop calls `checkNullGuards` with the default `fail-closed` outcome on a string `object` and on each array target. No finding on any target that declares `amount` nullable.
- **The `@example` passes the spec TSDoc gate.** RIGHT on reading. `hook-record-condition` judges it with `judge`, which is `validateExpression('value', source, { scope: 'record' })`. That gate checks syntax and roots only. `record.` is the only root used and `null` is a literal, so nothing new can be refused. The quoted form still opens with a quoted expression, so `inlineExampleSource` extracts it. Its CI job is still running.
- **Token growth.** RIGHT. The approvals reference goes from 22883 to 22908 bytes, which is ceil(/4) 5721 to 5727 tokens. The ratchet row on main is 5730, and `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is untouched. No deletions, so no deletion homes are owed.
- **Eval sweep.** RIGHT, nothing owed. The automation evals are three files. `flows-triggers-approvals.json` case 3 and `evals/approvals/test-revise-loop.md` (the `budget` past 100000 prompt) assert only the approval shape. No `expected_output` or `must_contain` spells an ordering comparison on `amount` or `budget`. `integrations-declared.json` mentions `amount` only inside a node-value expression, which the gate does not judge.
- **No model identifier.** None appears in the diff, the changeset or the PR body. The waiver says "the project's default model".

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` and `'@objectstack/spec': patch` are right. The diff changes skill prose, one schema's doc and describe text, and a generated reference row. No behaviour moves and no accept set moves, so `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right. Both lines are line-initial in the changeset and in the PR body, with `Fixes #31206`. The changeset text matches the diff, and its claim that "the `e1`, `e4` and `e5` edge conditions pass as written" is true against the lint code (①). The changeset and hook.mdx are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. hook.mdx changes exactly one row, and that row is the new describe string verbatim.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1: four guarded sites narrowed to the start condition only.** Upheld on the code, not on the PR body's word. The ruling the body calls a "seat ruling" is not on the card, so this record judged it independently.
  - The start condition is evaluated before any node on every run. The lint presumes whatever it proves at every edge and `decision` branch, in every graph (①).
  - The card's Owed says "guard each comparison the way the formula skill teaches". The formula skill teaches exactly this presumption (SKILL.md L404). In the gate's sense, every comparison in the flow is now guarded.
  - `e1`, `e4` and `e5` pass the publish-time null-guard rule, and they pass `os validate` and the runtime publish gate alike.
- **Is `e5`'s `<=` honest?** Yes. A null `amount` makes the start condition false, so the flow never launches and neither branch is reached. For any non-null number, `> 500000` and `<= 500000` are complementary and mutually exclusive, so exactly one out-edge of `needs_director` runs. Between launch and the decision, `manager_review` has `lockRecord: true`, and the run's variables are seeded once per run. So nothing in this example can null `amount` mid-run.
- **Deviation 2: no "edges inherit the start guard" clause.** Accepted. The skill's frontmatter sends conditions and edge guards to objectstack-formula, which states the rule at L404. See nit N1.
- **Claim.** All 4 paths are inside the claim's file surface. The evals and the ratchet script are untouched. No breach.
- **Tier.** Tier H (`skills/**`, `packages/spec/**`). `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green. Landing needs `os-zhuang` or `hotlong`.
- **Model-tier waiver.** Stated in the body under the maintainer's standing order of 2026-11-03, naming no model.
- **Gates still running** (02:04Z): 21 jobs, listed in ①. This PASS is on the tree. Landing still needs them green.
- **`open_questions`.** The PR body carries none. Its "Other sites found" list is confirmed for filing. Each one is outside this card's claim:
  1. `content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx` L371-L372: edges `e2` / `e3` compare a declared-nullable `amount` (L312) behind an unguarded start condition. This is refused as written.
  2. `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` L145, `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx` L74, `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx` L119 / L356 / L394, `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx` L329, `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` L2473: all are refused wherever `amount` is nullable.
  3. `packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts` L180, and its four generated rows in `content/docs/references/data/validation.mdx`: spec lane.
  4. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.erasedArmMark-9830.test.tsx` L110 hand-copies the old describe string. The test reads its own constant, so it still passes, but it will lag the served text once this lands. UI lane.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. No should-fix. Both `hits` files hold against the code they cite and against the card's scenario. An agent that copies either example into an app whose `opportunity.amount` is nullable now gets metadata that `os build`, `os validate`, `os lint` and the runtime publish gate all accept.

- **skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md: holds.** The one guard on the start condition, spelled with `record.`, clears the trigger gate. Through `provenNonNullKeys` it also clears `e1`, `e4` and `e5` on both doors. I tried to break it and could not:
  - Nested regions: `presumed` reaches every graph.
  - A bare spelling: not used, so the publish gate's stricter reading does not bite.
  - A `decision` slot: there is none.
  - A mid-run null: blocked by `lockRecord`, and `e5` stays honest.
- **packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts: holds.**
  - The guarded form is accepted by the hook-condition null-guard gate on single and multi-target hooks.
  - It is accepted by the spec `@example` gate, `hook-record-condition`, which judges record-scoped syntax and roots.
  - The `@example` (single-quoted `'closed'`) and the `.describe()` (double-quoted `"closed"`) keep the quoting each one had before.
  - No other comparison in the file is unguarded.

Nits, all optional:

- **nit N1: the example no longer says why `e4` / `e5` need no guard.** A reader who lifts just the `e4` / `e5` pair into a flow with an unguarded start condition, or with no start condition, gets refused. The skill's frontmatter pointer to objectstack-formula covers this, and a clause would cost bytes the file does not have (3 tokens of headroom). So leaving it out is a defensible choice.
- **nit N2: the start condition fires on every update while `amount` is above 100000.** It has no `previous` transition guard, so each edit to a high-value opportunity can launch another approval run. This predates the PR and is outside the card. The file's own state-machine note shows the transition shape (`previous.x != … && record.x == …`). Ported to `amount`, that shape would need its own `previous.amount != null` guard to pass the gate.
